---
address: mongolia.geo.postalCode
description: Real Mongolian postal codes, every one of them from the Communications Regulatory Commission's own register at zipcode.mn — THIS IS A LIST OF ISSUED CODES AND NOT A FIVE-DIGIT PATTERN, which matters because most of the 90000 arrangements of five digits are not allocated to anywhere in Mongolia and a naive [0-9]{5} generator emits them anyway. The code is five digits and it is written AFTER the aimag or the capital on the last line of the address ("ULAANBAATAR 14201"), which is the opposite of the Soviet-era order Mongolia used before. Read the digits as three fields, not as a hierarchy of five: positions 1-2 are the aimag or the capital district, position 3 is the zone inside it, positions 4-5 the delivery block — so 14201 is Sukhbaatar duureg (14), zone 2, block 01. Codes are frequently printed with a four-digit organisation suffix after a hyphen (14201-0033 is the CRC's own office), and that suffix is NOT part of the postal code; a column sized at five characters will truncate it and a column that keeps it will not match this list. The first digit is a postal region and it does NOT ascend with geography: the capital is 1, the eastern aimags 2, the central belt 4, the Khangai 6 and the west 8, while 3, 5, 7 and 9 open nothing at all. This file carries the capital's 714 district codes and all 330 aimag soum-centre codes. That mix is deliberately capital-heavy because Mongolia is: about 46 per cent of the country lives in Ulaanbaatar, so a flat draw over aimag codes alone would put a synthetic population where Mongolians do not live. It is still a subset — the CRC register also lists bag-level codes beneath each soum centre, which are omitted — so a code here is real but is not necessarily the code for the street you paired it with. If a config needs the code to agree with the place, filter on the leading two digits: 12 to 18 are the capital's districts (12 Baganuur and Bagakhangai and Nalaikh, 13 Bayanzurkh, 14 Sukhbaatar, 15 Chingeltei, 16 Bayangol, 17 Khan-Uul, 18 Songinokhairkhan) and 21 to 85 are the aimags, so drawing this file flat beside mongolia.geo.district will put a Selenge code on an Ulaanbaatar address about two times in three.
